# template-manifest.txt — WHO OWNS WHAT in your office
#
# The law this file exists to enforce:
#
#     Factory updates the operating system.
#     It does not redecorate the customer's office.
#
# The factory-update workflow reads THIS file — your copy — and syncs only what
# it names, always as a pull request you review and merge. Every managed path
# carries an owner, and the owner decides what an update is allowed to do to it.
#
# ── The two owners ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   core <path>     FACTORY-OWNED. The machinery: the update engine and its
#                   tests, the runtime, the stable contracts, the four thin seat
#                   loaders. Updates arrive by OVERWRITE, every run. Keeping
#                   these current is the whole point of an update — if you edit
#                   one, the next update will propose taking it back (use "!"
#                   below if you mean to keep your version).
#
#   office <path>   OFFICE-OWNED AFTER CREATION. The defaults: seat boot
#                   material, grounding, overrides, local doctrine, mission
#                   packs. The Factory SEEDS one of these only when your office
#                   does not have it yet, and NEVER writes it again. If the
#                   upstream default later improves, the update PR NAMES the
#                   file as a migration proposal — and still does not write it.
#                   Your customisation is safe by architecture, not by your
#                   having remembered to protect it.
#
#   <path>          A bare line with no owner means `core`. Manifests written
#                   before ownership existed keep working exactly as they did.
#
#   !<path>         PROTECTED — never written, whatever its owner. This is your
#                   own local opt-out for a `core` file you have deliberately
#                   made your own.
#
# Anything NOT listed here is yours alone: never seeded, never touched, never
# mentioned. Your journal, your specs, your roster, your company knowledge, and
# any file you add.
#
# One path per line. A trailing slash means "the whole folder." Lines starting
# with # are comments.
#
# ── Which rule applies to a file: the LONGEST match wins ─────────────────────
# The most specific rule decides, so a broad folder can be office-owned while
# something narrow inside it stays Factory-owned. That is exactly how the seat
# loaders work below. Order in this file does not matter — only specificity.
#
# ── Two things the sync can never do to you ──────────────────────────────────
#   • It never DELETES. A file of yours the Factory has never heard of is left
#     alone, not removed. (An earlier version `rm -rf`'d each managed folder and
#     re-copied it, which silently deleted every office-only file inside.)
#   • It never overwrites an `office` path, and never writes a `!` path.


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# FACTORY-OWNED — the operating system
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

core CLAUDE.md
core FROM-HQ.md
core MECHANICAL-RULES.md
core README.md
core THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
core VERSIONS.md
core .github/CONTRIBUTING.md
core .github/SECURITY.md
core .github/template-version.txt

# The updater's own engine. .github/workflows/factory-update.yml EXECUTES
# scripts/factory-sync.sh (the copying) and scripts/sync-selftest.sh (the proof,
# run before every sync). The workflow and the code it runs are ONE subsystem:
# if the scripts are not managed, a fix to the sync engine lands upstream and
# stops at your door in silence, while your workflow keeps running the old one.
# Factory-owned here so the two can never drift apart.
core scripts/

core guides/
core hosting/
core inbox/drop/README.md
core journal/README.md
core missions/README.md
core specs/README.md
core specialists/
core templates/
core tokens/
core versions/
core onboarding/
core skills/README.md
core skills/factory-coach/
core skills/factory-render-verify/
core skills/factory-retro/
core skills/factory-security/
core skills/factory-update/
core skills/skill-creator/


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OFFICE-OWNED — defaults that become yours the moment they land
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The seats. Your team's boot material — the prompts, the grounding, the
# overrides, the local doctrine — is what you adapt as your office learns, and
# it is the single most customised material in any office. It is yours.
#
# The four thin LOADERS inside those folders stay Factory-owned: they are the
# small stable cards installed in Claude's settings that do nothing but point at
# this repo. They are a contract, not content, and they must keep working when
# the boot material behind them changes. The longest-match rule is what lets
# both statements be true at once — look at any pair below.
office seats/_shared/
office seats/coach/
core   seats/coach/coach-boot/
office seats/cowork/
core   seats/cowork/cowork-boot/
office seats/designer/
core   seats/designer/designer-boot/
office seats/worker/
core   seats/worker/worker-boot/

# Your grounding — what your seats read to know your world.
office grounding/

# The mission packs. A shipped mission is a starting point you rewrite for the
# way your office actually works; an update should never take your version back.
office missions/design-guide/
office missions/first-app/
office missions/first-website/
office missions/organize-my-business/
office missions/website-overhaul/


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Deliberately absent — never seeded, never synced, never mentioned:
#   FACTORY.md            (carries your roster and your names)
#   journal.md            (your team's memory — the Factory's own news rides
#                          the managed FROM-HQ.md instead, never journal.md)
#   journal/archive/      (your history)
#   specs/                (your plans; only its README is managed)
#   .github/guardrails-denylist.txt  (your private-name denylist)
#   .github/heartbeat-watch.txt      (your own nightly watch list)
#   .github/workflows/    (a repo's automation can't be rewritten by its
#                          own automation — workflow changes arrive as a
#                          note in the update PR for an Engineer seat to apply.
#                          This is the ONE part of the updater that cannot be
#                          synced. Its engine, scripts/, is Factory-owned above,
#                          so the hand-carry is the workflow file alone — and
#                          guides/SAFE-UPDATE-BOOTSTRAP.md is the order to do
#                          it in, for an office that still has the old one.)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
